rows.summary: Kafka broker lakehouse-dual-role-0 is Running/Ready but network-isolated (Prometheus cannot scrape it, Loki has no logs from it), leaving 60 under-replicated partitions and zero fault-tolerance margin. A Chaos Mesh experiment deployed ~133 min ago (and updated again 15–33 min ago) is the almost-certain cause — do not restart the broker; escalate to stop the chaos experiment.

Kafka broker lakehouse-dual-role-0 is Running/Ready in Kubernetes but completely unreachable on the network — Prometheus cannot scrape it, its logs are inaccessible, and 60 partitions are under-replicated. A Chaos Mesh deployment ~133 minutes ago (coinciding with all pods crashing at exit_code 255 ~129 min ago) is the likely cause of a lingering network fault on broker-0. Brokers 1 and 2 are healthy; no partitions are offline or under min-ISR, so writes continue but with zero fault-tolerance margin.

Kafka broker lakehouse-dual-role-0 is Running/Ready but network-isolated (metrics scraping failing, 60 under-replicated partitions, 0 active controllers). Root cause is almost certainly an active Chaos Mesh experiment — chaos-mesh-local was deployed ~133 min ago, exactly when all three brokers and the Flink job terminated (exit code 255). Do NOT restart the pod; escalate to whoever owns the chaos experiment to stop it.

Flink checkpoint failures were triggered by a TaskManager restart ~2 minutes ago; the job is already back to RUNNING/STABLE with successful checkpoints and the alert should self-clear shortly. Consumer lag is 650 events and draining.

Flink checkpoint failures were caused by a TaskManager abrupt shutdown ~2 minutes ago (likely a Chaos Mesh experiment), triggering a brief job restart. The Flink job is now STABLE/RUNNING and completing checkpoints again; the system is self-healing.
Flink checkpoint failures caused by a Chaos Mesh-induced taskmanager restart ~2 minutes ago; the job is already RUNNING/STABLE with 25 completed checkpoints in the last 5 min and is self-healing.

Node `lakehouse-worker` (zone-a) is unreachable, taking Kafka broker `lakehouse-dual-role-2` and the Flink job manager with it. Kafka is serving on 2/3 brokers with 60 under-replicated partitions and zero margin — one more failure would halt writes. Escalate to the infra team to recover or replace the node.

Node lakehouse-worker (zone-a) is unreachable, taking down Kafka broker lakehouse-dual-role-2, the Flink job manager, and the ingestion service pod hosted on it. All 60 under-replicated partitions are present but writes continue (2 ISR brokers meet min.insync.replicas=2 — no headroom). Escalate to restore or replace the node.

Node `lakehouse-worker` (zone-a) is unreachable, taking Kafka broker `lakehouse-dual-role-2` and the Flink job manager offline. The cluster is functional (0 offline partitions, min-ISR still met) but has zero fault-tolerance margin; Strimzi is also blocked from reconciling by a Kyverno webhook error.
